A {{convert|6|ft|5|in|m|adj=on}} tall [[shooting guard]] from [[Shreveport, Louisiana]], he last played with the [[Maine Red Claws]] of the [[NBA Development League]]. Thomas is now the basketball head coach of [[Rockhurst High School]]. ==College career== In his college career, Thomas set a KU record making 269 3-point field goals (that record was later broken by [[Jeff Boschee]]). He also holds the school record for 3-point field goals made in a conference game, connecting on eight of them in a game against [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas]] on January 10, 1998. ==Professional career== Thomas went [[undrafted]] after graduating from the [[University of Kansas]] in 1998. In 2001, Thomas averaged 27.6 points in 10 games for the [[Tanduay Rhum Masters]] under coach [[Derick Pumaren]] in the [[Philippine Basketball Association]]. In 2002–03, Thomas won the [[NBA Development League|NBDL]] Sportsmanship Award while playing for the Greenville Groove.[http://www.nba.com/dleague/nbdl/thomas_sportsmanship_030319.html Billy Thomas Selected as 2002–03 NBDL Sportsmanship Award Winner] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160610060216/http://www.nba.com/dleague/nbdl/thomas_sportsmanship_030319.html |date=June 10, 2016 }} He played for the [[Dakota Wizards]] of the [[Continental Basketball Association]] (CBA) and was named the [[Continental Basketball Association Newcomer of the Year Award|CBA Newcomer of the Year]] and a member of the All-CBA First Team in 2005.{{cite web |title=Billy Thomas minor league basketball statistics |url=https://www.statscrew.com/minorbasketball/stats/p-thomabil001 |website=Stats Crew |access-date=June 23, 2021}} He began his [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] career during the [[2004–05 NBA season|2004–2005 season]] by signing a 10-day contract with the [[New Jersey Nets]] on January 20, 2005. Thomas later signed a second 10-day contract and eventually was signed for the remainder of the season. He appeared in 25 games that year and averaged 3.7 points per game. On March 3, 2006, he signed a 10-day contract with the [[Washington Wizards]]. He played in 17 games and averaged 2.2 points per game. Thomas began the 2007–2008 season with the [[Colorado 14ers]] of the [[NBDL|D-League]]. In 27 games (27 starts), prior to his second NBA call-up, Thomas averaged 15.7 points, 3.4 rebounds and 3.7 assists per game. Thomas was selected to play in the 2008 D-League All-Star Game. On December 24, 2007, Thomas was signed to a ten-day contract with the [[New Jersey Nets]]. He played in four games with the Nets, scoring a total of two points. On February 22, 2008, Thomas was signed to a ten-day contract by the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] so they would have enough players to face the Washington Wizards that night, due to a depleted roster because of a blockbuster trade the day prior.[http://www.ohio.com/news/break_news/15874817.html Cavs sign minor-leaguers.] Thomas saw his first action as a Cavalier that very night, playing 19 minutes and scoring 9 points on three three-point shots. Thomas hoisted 11 three-point field goal attempts, his career high.[http://www.nba.com/playerfile/billy_thomas/game_by_game_stats.html Billy Thomas Profile.] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071229040922/http://www.nba.com/playerfile/billy_thomas/game_by_game_stats.html |date=December 29, 2007 }} On March 3, 2008, the Cavaliers signed Thomas to a second ten-day contract.[http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/news/dickens_thomas_080303.html Cavaliers Sign Dickens, Thomas To Second 10-Day Contracts.] His contract expired on March 13, 2008, allowing him to become a free agent. On March 20, 2008, Thomas returned to the Colorado 14ers. On April 16, 2008, the Cavaliers signed Thomas for the remainder of the season and the 2008 playoffs.[http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/news/thomas_signs_080416.html Cavaliers Sign Billy Thomas.] He played in seven regular-season games for the Cavaliers scoring 12 total points (on four three-point field goals made) grabbed two rebounds and made one steal. Thomas logged eight minutes over three playoff games. He scored three points (on a three-point field goal) and had a rebound, an assist and a steal. Thomas played for the Cavaliers' 2008 [[NBA Summer League]] team in [[Las Vegas Valley|Las Vegas]]. He started both games that he played and averaged five points, two rebounds, two assists, one steal and a half a block per game.[http://www.nba.com/summerleague2008/players/index.jsp?player=billy_thomas Billy Thomas Summer League Statistics.] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080815232601/http://www.nba.com/summerleague2008/players/index.jsp?player=billy_thomas |date=August 15, 2008 }} Thomas has played in numerous other leagues during his professional basketball career: the [[United States Basketball League|USBL]], the [[Continental Basketball Association|CBA]], the [[International Basketball League (1999–2001)|IBL]], the [[NBDL|D-League]], the [[Liga Nacional de Básquetbol|Argentine League]], the [[Serie A (basketball)|Italian League]], the [[Naša Sinalko Liga|Serbian League]], the [[Adriatic League]], the [[A1 Ethniki|Greek League]] and the [[ULEB Cup]]. On September 2, 2009, Thomas was drafted by the [[Maine Red Claws]] in the third round of the NBA Development League Expansion Draft.{{Citation needed|date=May 2016}} ==Coaching career== Thomas is the owner of the "Billy Thomas Hoops Academy", located in Kansas City, Missouri.{{Citation needed|date=May 2016}} Beginning in the 2010–2011 season, Thomas was the head coach of the boy's varsity basketball team at [[The Barstow School]] in Kansas City, Missouri.{{Cite web|url=http://www2.kusports.com/news/2010/oct/16/former-jayhawk-billy-thomas-accepts-high-school-co/|title=Former Jayhawk Billy Thomas accepts high school coaching position|website=KUsports.com|date=October 16, 2010 |access-date=May 28, 2016}} In the 2015–2016 season, the Barstow boys' basketball team was ranked first in the small school category by the [[Kansas City Star]].{{Cite web|url=http://www.kansascity.com/sports/high-school/article73536537.html|title=The Star's high school basketball final rankings|website=kansascity|access-date=May 28, 2016}} In 2021, he became the head coach for the [[Rockhurst High School]] basketball team.{{Cite
